transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’ve been really struggling with my eating lately, and it's getting hard to handle. I keep finding myself eating huge amounts of food in a very short time, and I feel like I completely lose control and just can't stop. I didn't really know what else to do, so I decided to come in today.
After these episodes, do you ever try to get rid of the food by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Yes, I do, and I feel so ashamed about it. I usually force myself to throw up right after, and I've also used laxatives or forced myself to exercise for hours to make up for it. I just get so panicked about gaining weight and don't know what else to do.
Do you feel that your self-worth is strongly tied to your weight or body shape, and are you very afraid of gaining weight?

Yes, completely. My entire self-worth is tied to the scale, and I feel like a total failure as a person if I gain even a single pound. I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight, and it's pretty much all I think about.
How long have these bingeing and purging episodes been going on?
It has been going on for about two years and four months now. I've been struggling with this cycle for such a long time, and it feels like it has completely taken over my life.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was Bulimia Nervosa, and the new information strongly supports it: recurrent binge eating, recurrent compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxatives, excessive exercise), intense fear of weight gain, and overvaluation of weight/shape for over two years. No evidence was provided for anorexia nervosa (no low body weight), binge-eating disorder (because compensatory behaviors are present), or another primary psychiatric disorder, so the candidate list remains unchanged.

final_diagnosis.reason: Recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control followed by compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative use, excessive exercise) and an overvaluation/fear of weight gain for over 2 years are classic for bulimia nervosa. Binge-eating disorder is less likely because compensatory behaviors are present, and anorexia nervosa is less likely because the transcript does not indicate significantly low body weight.
